questions.question: What can you do with an improperly placarded vehicle?

options.text: It can only be moved in an emergency.
It can be driven short distances.
It can be driven if it does not contain radioactive materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can only be moved in an emergency.
questions.explanation: A vehicle carrying hazardous materials must have proper placards. An improperly placarded vehicle can only be driven in an emergency to protect life or property.

questions.question: Which material may need a transport index?
questions.explanation: Some radioactive materials need a transport index. This number shows how much control is needed during transport. The total transport index for all cargo in one vehicle cannot be more than 50.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in a trailer, how should you clean it?

options.text: Leave it to air dry without washing.

questions.explanation: Any part of a vehicle that touches corrosive liquids must be washed thoroughly with water.

questions.question: What is important to know about transporting radioactive materials?

options.text: Radiation spreads from the package and can reach other packages nearby.
The package must be transported in the cab.
The package must be loaded on its side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation spreads from the package and can reach other packages nearby.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads from each radioactive package and can reach nearby packages. The number of packages you can load together is controlled to manage this risk.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials containers, what should you NOT use?
questions.explanation: Protect hazardous materials containers. Never use equipment that could damage containers, such as hooks.

questions.question: Which agency helps respond to chemical hazards?

options.text: The United Center for Chemical Assistance

questions.explanation: The National Response Center helps coordinate emergency response to chemical hazards. Contact them if there is a hazardous materials spill.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, where should you NOT park your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Do not park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Also do not park within 5 feet of the road.

questions.question: A person supervising tank loading or unloading must do all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Stay within 25 feet of the tank
Know the hazards of the materials

questions.explanation: The supervisor must be alert, have a clear view of the tank, stay within 25 feet, know the material hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed. Wearing a chemical suit is not required.

questions.question: How should shipping papers be placed in the cab?

options.text: Easily visible to anyone entering the cab

questions.correctAnswerText: Easily visible to anyone entering the cab
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or in a place the driver can reach while wearing a seat belt. They must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: What do you need to know to choose the right placard?

options.text: The hazard class of the materials
The type of container holding the materials

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard class of the materials
questions.explanation: To pick the right placards, you must know the hazard class of the materials, how much hazardous material you are shipping, and the total weight of all hazardous materials in your vehicle.

questions.question: If cargo is leaking, what should you do?

options.text: Touch the leaking material to find out what it is.
Check the shipping papers and labels to identify the cargo.
Spray the leaking containers with water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the shipping papers and labels to identify the cargo.
questions.explanation: If you find a leak in hazardous materials, use the shipping papers, labels, or package location to identify what is leaking. Do not touch the material.

questions.question: What is important to know when transporting radioactive materials?

options.text: Radiation passes through to nearby packages.
The packages should be carried in the cab.
The packages should be loaded on their side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation passes through to nearby packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation from radioactive packages spreads out and reaches nearby packages. Because of this, there is a limit to how many radioactive packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: What must be in a vehicle transporting chlorine?
questions.explanation: A driver transporting chlorine must have an approved gas mask in the vehicle. The driver must also have an emergency kit to control leaks from the cargo tank.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in the trailer, how should it be cleaned?
questions.explanation: Any part of a vehicle exposed to corrosive material must be thoroughly washed with water.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Push on the tires to feel the pressure.

questions.explanation: Check each tire before every trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only proper way to check tire pressure.

questions.question: What should you do when loading or unloading explosive materials?

options.text: Use sharp-pointed tools to open packages.

questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading explosives. Never drop, throw, or roll packages containing explosives.

questions.question: Why can opening trailer doors during a cargo fire make it worse?

options.text: It allows oxygen into the trailer.
It adds moisture to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows oxygen into the trailer.
questions.explanation: During a cargo fire, opening the doors lets oxygen in. This can cause the fire to flare up and spread.

questions.question: What is the minimum fire extinguisher rating for placarded vehicles?
questions.explanation: Placarded vehicles must have a fire extinguisher with a UL rating of 10 B:C or higher.

questions.question: Who can transport hazardous materials?

options.text: Any driver, if the total weight is under 50 pounds.
Any driver in a rural area.
A driver with a CDL and HazMat endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver with a CDL and HazMat endorsement.
questions.explanation: You need a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that transports hazardous materials.

questions.question: Which agency checks you before issuing a HazMat endorsement?
questions.explanation: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) conducts a background check before you can get or renew a HazMat endorsement.

questions.question: Shipping papers:

options.text: Are not needed for most shipments.
Should be stored in a special compartment in the cab.
Can be kept as a digital file.

questions.explanation: Shipping papers are required for all hazardous materials shipments. They tell drivers and workers about the dangers of the cargo.

questions.question: Where should hazardous materials shipping papers NOT be kept?

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's side door
In a pouch on the passenger's side door
Within reach of the driver while the seat belt is fastened
On the driver's seat while the driver is outside of the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's side door
questions.explanation: While driving, shipping papers must be in a pouch on the driver's door or within the driver's reach. If the driver leaves the vehicle, papers should be on the driver's seat.

questions.question: Load hazardous materials:
questions.explanation: Always load hazardous materials away from heat sources. Some materials cannot be loaded in spaces with heaters.

questions.question: A hazardous materials placard is shaped like a:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: A material's hazard class shows:

options.text: The risks associated with the material.
The amount of packaging required to make the shipment.
The location on the trailer where items may be placed.
How the material should be loaded and unloaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: The risks associated with the material.
questions.explanation: There are nine hazard classes. Each hazard class shows what risks the material has.

questions.question: Hazardous materials placards are usually shaped like a:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: Where can you find identification numbers for chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook.
questions.explanation: The DOT Emergency Response Guidebook lists all hazardous chemicals and their identification numbers.

questions.question: How long must shippers keep a copy of shipping papers?
questions.explanation: Shippers must keep a copy of hazardous materials shipping papers for at least two years after the carrier accepts the materials. For hazardous waste, the time is three years.

questions.question: Which material may need a transport index?
questions.explanation: Some radioactive materials need a transport index. This number shows how much control the material needs during transport. The total transport index for all cargo in one vehicle cannot be more than 50.

questions.question: Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table lists:
questions.explanation: Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table shows the proper shipping names and descriptions of regulated materials.
